findings.failure_scenario: With `[local].remote_host = "gpu"` (an SSH alias) and a provider base_url of `http://gpu.lan:8080/v1` that needs an API key, `local up` reports endpoint unreachable and never enables the provider.

findings.title: Over the source budget, with extra UI surface
findings.detail: The source diff is about +181/−85, against a budget of about 120 mostly-deleted lines. It adds new UI reporting of unavailable references and changes the RuntimeCatalog removal semantics, both beyond the minimum needed for old records to render and resume.
findings.failure_scenario: Not applicable (review scope).

gold.summary: Raw process output is cut before gate credential redaction can match a boundary-spanning secret.

findings.title: Verify-prompt redaction assertions are vacuous
findings.detail: verifyPrompt only renders each check's name, command and verdict, never `result.output` or `failures`. The new `not.toContain(gateCredential)` assertions would pass with or without redaction.
findings.failure_scenario: Remove the redactGateOutput call in run.ts and this test still passes.

gold.summary: JSON escaping lets ordinary logged credentials evade literal gate-output redaction.
Line callbacks store pieces of multiline credentials in failure excerpts.

findings.title: Multiline registered credentials survive failure excerpt redaction
findings.detail:
Redaction runs separately on each line, so a registered credential containing a newline never matches. A direct runGates probe returned a redacted output tail but the complete credential in failures, which is persisted in gate artifacts and state. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {extractFailures} from "./src/gates/failures.ts"; import {registerCredential} from "./src/util/proc.ts"; const secret="synthetic-multiline-credential
second-secret-line-123"; registerCredential("MULTILINE_TOKEN",secret); const failures=extractFailures("error: "+secret+"
(fail) assertion
"); if (failures?.includes(secret)) throw new Error("Registered credential survives failure excerpt redaction");' Output: er
findings.failure_scenario: A check prints a registered multiline credential in its diagnostic block, followed by '(fail) assertion'. The complete secret survives in GateResult.failures despite being removed from GateResult.output.

gold.summary: Redacting the carry early emits suffixes of overlapping registered credentials.
ANSI stripping after framing and tail cuts leaves accidental credential fragments visible.

findings.title: Whole prompt inputs (including the patch under review) go through gate-output sanitization
findings.detail: `implementPrompt`, `reviewPrompt` and `verifyPrompt` now run their entire input through `redactGateData`, which applies `stripVTControlCharacters` and credential redaction to every string. That includes the request prompt, the spec, the implementer report and the inline `patch` of the change under review, not just the gate results. The request asked for redaction once, where `runGates` builds the result, so every consumer gets text that is already clean. Here the review model is shown a different diff from the one that will merge.
findings.failure_scenario: A change adds a file containing raw ESC terminal sequences, for example a hidden `\x1b[8m` concealment sequence or OSC escapes in a string literal. `reviewPrompt` strips them from `patch`, so the reviewer sees a sanitized diff and cannot flag the control characters the change actually introduces.

findings.title: Artifact endpoint re-serializes JSON artifacts compactly and alters non-gate artifacts
findings.detail: `redactGateArtifact` runs `JSON.parse` and then `JSON.stringify` with no indent on every artifact that parses as JSON. Pretty-printed artifacts such as `gates-N.json`, `baseline-gates.json` and the review-shadow JSON are written with `JSON.stringify(x, null, 2)` and are now served on one line, which the UI shows as raw text. The replacer also adds a `confinementError` field to any object that has `ok` and `output` keys, and `stripVTControlCharacters` is applied to every artifact, including `diff.patch` and `spec.md`.
findings.failure_scenario: `GET /api/runs/:id/artifacts/gates-1.json` used to return indented JSON and now returns a single minified line with extra `confinementError` fields.

findings.title: Every API response and SSE message is deep-cloned and rewritten
findings.detail: `json()` and `sse()` now pass all payloads, including run lists, stats, catalog and events, through `redactGateData`. That is a JSON round trip, a VT strip and a credential scan on every string, plus the `ok`/`output` object rewrite. It is unrequested scope, adds a per-message cost on hot SSE paths, and silently changes the shape of any unrelated object that happens to have `ok` and `output` fields.
findings.failure_scenario: A run event stream carrying large payloads gets a full JSON parse, stringify and regex pass per message. An endpoint returning `{ok, output}` gains a `confinementError` key it never had.

findings.title: MCP privacy filter now withholds any field containing "[redacted]"; unrequested and untested
findings.detail: `loadOutputPrivacy` now returns "[withheld: private text]" for any string that contains the literal "[redacted]". After this change, gate output that had a credential redacted is dropped entirely from MCP responses, losing all diagnostics. Unrelated text that mentions "[redacted]" (titles, reasons, harness tool output that was already redacted) is also withheld. No test in the diff covers this change.
findings.failure_scenario: A land check fails with output containing one redacted credential. An MCP client asking for the land reason or run status gets "[withheld: private text]" instead of the failure excerpt.

findings.title: New `stdoutTruncated`/`stderrTruncated` result fields are unused
findings.detail: `ProcResult` gains per-stream truncation flags, and `hardening.test.ts` tests them, but nothing in `src` reads them. This is extra churn against a budget of about 30 lines.
findings.failure_scenario: There is no runtime failure; this is dead API surface.

gold.summary: An incomplete terminal escape consumes part of a credential before it can be matched.
Terminal-control stripping changes with chunk boundaries and loses state at the hold limit.

findings.title: Overlapping credential matches make the streaming buffer unbounded
findings.detail: The cut-adjustment loop repeatedly retreats across overlapping matches, potentially reaching the start of the entire pending buffer. With credential `aaaaaaaa` and repeated `a` output, nothing is emitted until the stream ends, so tailLimit does not bound retention. A mocked subprocess emitting sixteen 1 MiB chunks with tailLimit=100 retained 17,901,021 additional live heap bytes before ending, although the returned result was only 100 characters. Continued output can exhaust daemon memory and repeatedly rescan an increasingly large buffer.
findings.failure_scenario: Register `aaaaaaaa` as a credential, then run a gate or deploy command that continuously prints `a` without closing stdout. The pending buffer grows with all output despite the configured tail limit.

gold.summary: Nesting Seatbelt around internally sandboxed CLIs prevents tool-enabled invocations from starting.
Scanning ordinary agent output for sandbox diagnostics can discard successful invocations.
Ordinary gate output mentioning sandbox failures can turn a successful check into a confinement error.
The live confinement smoke accepts refusal even when enforcement should work.

findings.title: Provide writable isolated state for the confined Codex CLI
findings.detail: The new outer profile denies writes outside cwd and scratch, but the CLI still inherits its normal HOME/CODEX_HOME. Normal invocations remain persistent because --ephemeral is added only for privateSession. Codex therefore cannot create its session rollout and other persistent state under ~/.codex. Unlike the corresponding Claude change, this wrapper does not accommodate the CLI's persistence requirements. The substitute smoke executable never attempts those writes.
findings.failure_scenario: On a host where confinement preflights succeed, a normal tool-enabled Codex invocation starts with privateSession unset and attempts to create its rollout under ~/.codex; the outer write policy denies it and the invocation fails.

findings.title: Detect executed substitutions inside double-quoted shell arguments
findings.detail: Double-quoted tokens are treated as opaque literals, although command substitutions inside them execute. Consequently echo "$(kill -TERM 123)" produces no warning, feed item, or report count. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import { strict as assert } from "node:assert"; import { signalCommand } from "./src/harness/signals.ts"; assert.equal(signalCommand("echo \"$(kill -TERM 123)\""), true, "executed command substitution must be detected");'. Output: AssertionError: executed command substitution must be detected; false !== true.
findings.failure_scenario: Either harness emits a shell tool call containing echo "$(kill -TERM 123)". The shell executes kill, but signalCommand returns false and no signal warning is recorded.

gold.summary: LFS exemptions permit missing payloads and pointer replacements containing archives.
The limited text sample exempts a TAR whose first binary byte lies beyond the sample.
The WebP inspector rejects valid lossy VP8 images.

findings.title: Restore all explicitly approved inert media extensions
findings.detail: The allowlist omits PDF, MP4, BMP, AVIF, TIFF, HEIC, PSD, EOT, several audio/video formats, and all requested 3D formats. These now produce binary-content blocks, contrary to the requested list and explicit PDF/MP4 acceptance checks. The new tests even assert that complete PDFs block. Verification command: bun -e 'import {strict as assert} from "node:assert"; import {isInertMedia} from "./src/gates/media.ts"; import {readFileSync} from "node:fs"; const f=JSON.parse(readFileSync("test/fixtures/media/files.json","utf8")); assert.equal(isInertMedia("document.pdf",Buffer.from(f["0.pdf"],"base64")),true,"complete PDF must be exempt");'. Output: AssertionError: complete PDF must be exempt; false !
findings.failure_scenario: A request adds or edits an ordinary binary PDF or MP4 without Allow: binary; the audit blocks it.

findings.title: Do not reject ordinary media metadata
findings.detail: The new parser rejects valid PNG tEXt chunks, so ordinary image descriptions remove the exemption. Similar restrictions reject JPEG EXIF and MP3 ID3 metadata. This introduces content restrictions beyond the requested extension split and makes normal inert assets require an allowance. Verification command: bun -e 'import {strict as assert} from "node:assert"; import {isInertMedia} from "./src/gates/media.ts"; import {readFileSync} from "node:fs"; const f=JSON.parse(readFileSync("test/fixtures/media/files.json","utf8")); const b=Buffer.from(f["0.png"],"base64"); const p=Buffer.from("Comment\0ordinary image description"); const c=Buffer.alloc(p.length+12); c.writeUInt32BE(p.length); c.write("tE
findings.failure_scenario: An otherwise accepted PNG gains a valid tEXt chunk containing an ordinary description; isInertMedia returns false and the audit blocks the image.

gold.summary: Detached descendants survive invocation cleanup and keep modifying the worktree.
Process cleanup returns while owned descendants are still alive.
Discarding changes replaces the cleanup error that should trigger round recovery.

findings.title: Process-group cleanup still lets detached descendants survive
findings.detail: The new exit handler kills and polls only the invocation's original process group. A descendant started with detached:true (or setsid) belongs to another group and survives after runProcess resolves, violating the required whole-tree cleanup. Reproduction command: bun --eval 'import {runProcess} from "./src/util/proc.ts"; const r=await runProcess({cmd:[process.execPath,"-e",`const c=require("child_process").spawn("sleep",["3"],{detached:true,stdio:"ignore"});c.unref();console.log(c.pid)`],cwd:process.cwd(),env:process.env}); const pid=Number(r.stdout.trim()); console.log("descendant alive after return:",process.kill(pid,0)); process.kill(pid,"SIGKILL");' Output: descendant alive after return
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer launches a detached background test runner that writes into node_modules. The invocation ends, but the runner survives and races with worktree cleanup.

gold.summary: Shutdown drops an already claimed descendant when its parent exits.
Holdout snapshot deletion proceeds despite unconfirmed descendant termination.
Production scratch directories are never registered as process ownership roots.
Replacing a descendant environment removes it from invocation discovery.

findings.title: Do not infer process ownership from birth time and cwd
findings.detail: An unrelated orphan born during an invocation is classified as its descendant solely because it shares the working directory. Cleanup consequently signals processes belonging to other callers. A standalone reproduction launched an independent, unmarked /bin/sleep through a separate launcher while the invocation waited. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/review-377.test.ts". Output: '(fail) independent orphan survives invocation cleanup', 'Expected: true', 'Received: false'.
findings.failure_scenario: Another caller launches a detached platform process in the same directory while runProcess is active; its launcher exits. Invocation cleanup kills that unrelated orphan.

findings.title: Retain group-based cleanup when descendants replace their environment
findings.detail: Session/group membership is considered only when environment data is absent. A child with a readable replacement environment lacking the invocation marker is ignored even when it remains in the invocation's process group. runProcess then reports successful shutdown while that child remains alive. This regresses the previous unconditional group kill. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/review-377.test.ts". Output: '(fail) same-group child with replaced environment is stopped', 'Expected: false', 'Received: true'.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer spawns a background Bun process with env: {PATH: '/usr/bin:/bin'}, stdio: 'ignore', and no detachment, then exits. The child survives runProcess returning and can continue writing during cleanup.

gold.summary: Pre-aborted shutdown with failed leader inspection references timer cleanup before initialization and never settles.

findings.title: Do not infer process ownership from working directory and birth time
findings.detail: The orphan fallback claims unrelated processes merely because they started during the invocation and share its working directory. Cleanup then signals those processes. A direct reproduction launched an independent orphan from the reviewer process while runProcess was active. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-377.ts". Output: {"invocationExit":0,"unrelatedPid":34184,"unrelatedAlive":false}, followed by 'ASSERTION FAILED: unrelated orphan must survive invocation cleanup'.
findings.failure_scenario: Another task or user starts a detached process in the same checkout while an invocation runs; its launcher exits. Invocation cleanup kills that unrelated process.

findings.title: Detached descendants can still outlive invocation cleanup
findings.detail: Discovery loses descendants that detach, replace their environment, and change directory outside the invocation roots before their parent exits. runProcess then reports successful termination while the child continues writing into the worktree by absolute path. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-377-escape.ts". Output: {"invocationExit":0,"descendantPid":39246,"descendantAlive":true}, followed by 'ASSERTION FAILED: invocation descendant must be stopped before runProcess returns'. This leaves the original cleanup race possible and violates the whole-process-tree requirement.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer launches a detached background shell with a clean environment and an external working directory. The shell writes to an absolute worktree path, and the implementer exits. Cleanup proceeds while the writer remains alive.

gold.summary: The reader loopback policy cannot match the intended socket access.
An allow-default reader policy weakens the established confinement boundary.

findings.title: Disable the HTTP idle timeout for verification commands
findings.detail: Bun.serve defaults to a 10-second idle timeout. This endpoint buffers its JSON response until executeReaderCommand finishes, so commands lasting longer than 10 seconds lose their HTTP connection regardless of the configured subprocess and MCP tool timeouts. The request abort signal also feeds into subprocess cancellation. Ordinary verification suites can therefore still fail as environment-blocked.
findings.failure_scenario: A verifier calls the reader command tool with a test suite that takes 20 seconds. No HTTP response data is sent during execution, so Bun closes the connection after approximately 10 seconds and the verifier receives a transport failure instead of the test result.

gold.summary: Free-text claim detection still lets model wording steer gate-evidence substitution.

findings.title: Unrelated skipped tests disable the loopback fallback
findings.detail: The clean-result predicate rejects any skipped file, and applyGateEvidence requires every gate to satisfy it. Limitless deliberately skips real Seatbelt tests inside confined gates, so its successful suite cannot attest to a fully passing loopback test in another file. The reported verification block therefore remains for this repository. Reproduction command: bun test --preload "$TMPDIR/review-zod.ts" "$TMPDIR/review-gate-repro.test.ts". Output: '(fail) unrelated skipped file', 'Expected: "met"', 'Received: "blocked"'. The temporary preload selects the installed Zod v4.
findings.failure_scenario: Confined bun test passes test/loopback.test.ts but skips a nested Seatbelt test in test/sandbox.test.ts. The reader cannot bind loopback, and the engine rejects the otherwise valid gate evidence, leaving verification blocked.

findings.title: Independent evidence mentioning a gate is discarded
findings.detail: gateClaim matches any standalone occurrence of 'gate', even when the verifier describes independently observed behavior. Sanitization then changes a met criterion to blocked and deletes its evidence. Reproduction command: bun test --preload "$TMPDIR/review-zod.ts" "$TMPDIR/review-gate-repro.test.ts". Output: '(fail) independent evidence mentioning gate', 'Expected: "met"', 'Received: "blocked"'. The evidence was 'bun test test/loopback.test.ts: 1 pass, 0 fail. This directly exercises the gate profile.'
findings.failure_scenario: A verifier successfully runs a targeted test and reports that it exercises the gate profile. With no substitutable gate record, the engine converts the successful observation into an environment block and can terminate the run as needs_human.

gold.summary: Matching a successful command does not establish the observation required by the criterion.
Targeted Bun evidence can satisfy a criterion without proof that any tests ran.

findings.title: Unrelated platform skips disable loopback gate evidence
findings.detail: The global skipped-test rejection prevents substitution even when retained coverage proves the required loopback file passed. This repository's confined gates deliberately skip real Seatbelt tests, so its normal full-suite gate results cannot resolve the reported verification block. Exact reproduction command: bun --eval 'import {applyGateEvidence as apply} from "./src/pipeline/gate-evidence.ts"; const sha="a".repeat(40); const actual=apply({criteria:[{id:"AC-1",status:"blocked",blockedReason:"sandbox"}]},{acceptance_criteria:[{id:"AC-1",how_to_verify:"bun test test/loopback.test.ts"}]},{scenarios:[]},sha,{stageId:12,sha,checks:[{verdict:"pass",blocking:false,testCommand:"bun test",result:{o
findings.failure_scenario: The factory runs this repository's configured bun test gate under LIMITLESS_CONFINED=1. The loopback test passes, real Seatbelt tests skip as designed, and the verifier reports its loopback sandbox block. Substitution is refused and the run still ends needs_human.

gold.summary: Manual push reloads mutable clone configuration after its final validation snapshot.
Inherited Git configuration causes validation and push to inspect different settings.
An exact upstream URL requirement rejects supported forks and alternate origin spellings.

findings.title: Protect the delivery and land-queue pushes too
findings.detail: Neither pushBranch nor pushExistingBranch excludes repository config or overrides command-running settings. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-push.ts"` against a local bare remote with a repository-scoped URL rewrite and protocol.ext.allow=always produced `delivery: marker=true` and `land: marker=true`; both remote SHAs still matched the pinned SHA. These two explicitly required push paths remain vulnerable.
findings.failure_scenario: PR code plants a URL rewrite to an ext helper that creates a marker and forwards to the local Git transport. Subsequent delivery or land-queue publication executes that helper.

findings.title: Exclude untrusted config during the actual push
findings.detail: The final push still uses origin and reads live repository config. Validation and snapshot comparison only inspect earlier state; they do not prevent a background process started by unconfined PR checks from planting remote.origin.receivepack after the last snapshot. The actual push also lacks the required protocol.ext.allow=never override.
findings.failure_scenario: A background child of bun run check updates repository config after config_after is captured but before git push reads it. The push then executes the planted receivepack command.

findings.title: Do not reject harmless repository settings
findings.detail: The new allowlist blocks ordinary repository-local identity settings, preventing landing before checks even start. Invoking validate_repository_config in a temporary repository with a valid origin and local user.name/user.email returned exit 1 and printed `Repository git config key user.name is not allowed; refusing to land` and the equivalent user.email error. The request requires ignoring untrusted push settings, not banning unrelated repository configuration.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator configures their commit identity locally rather than globally and runs land-pr.sh on an otherwise valid checkout.

findings.title: Allow sufficient time for the expanded subprocess tests
findings.detail: `bun test test/land-pr.test.ts` finished with `45 pass`, `18 fail`, and `14 errors`; all 18 failed cases exceeded the default 5000ms timeout, causing subsequent assertion failures. Running `bun test --timeout 30000 test/land-pr.test.ts -t 'tampering: redirect$'` passed in 8130ms. The four receivepack/SSH/helper/include cases also passed with the longer timeout, taking 6.7–8.1 seconds each.
findings.failure_scenario: The normal test command runs these expanded cases on a slower or loaded macOS machine and terminates them before validation or publication completes.

gold.summary: The loop detector aborts before the threshold call can return evidence of progress.

findings.title: Wait for the threshold call’s result before committing to a loop stop
findings.detail: observe() returns the stop reason before the current call’s result arrives. Both harnesses immediately abort and permanently set stuckReason, so observeResult() cannot rescue a sixth call whose output changes. Reproduced with command: bun -e 'import { strict as assert } from "node:assert"; import { LoopDetector } from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d = new LoopDetector(100); for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) { assert.equal(d.observe("shell", "poll", String(i)), null); d.observeResult(String(i), "waiting"); } const reason = d.observe("shell", "poll", "5"); d.observeResult("5", "1 test passed"); assert.equal(reason, null, "a changed sixth result must not stop a progressing poll");'. Output: Asserti
findings.failure_scenario: Five identical polling calls return 'waiting'. The sixth poll returns '1 test passed', but its tool_call event has already triggered cancellation and marked the run stuck.

gold.summary: A completed parallel call is classified as repetitive before unresolved predecessors establish progress.

findings.title: An unresolved sixth call no longer triggers loop detection
findings.detail: This condition suppresses detection until another tool call invokes reconcile(true) or the process exits and finish() runs. If the sixth identical call hangs without returning a result, neither happens while the invocation remains active. The agent consequently runs until an unrelated inactivity or invocation timeout, whereas the request explicitly preserves today's counting for still-running calls. A direct bun -e probe with five identical completed calls followed by one unresolved identical call returned null for all six observe() calls.
findings.failure_scenario: Five identical shell calls return 'waiting'; a sixth identical shell call starts and never returns. No further tool calls arrive. The repeated-call detector never aborts the active invocation.

gold.summary: Increasing panel test deadlines leaves the underlying parallel Git race undiagnosed.
Factory gate environment construction discards the configured test worker override.

findings.title: Supply the required measurements for the parallel default
findings.detail: The change selects four workers and doubles the flaky panel test's deadline, but provides none of the requested measurements: serial versus 4/6/8 workers, wall and CPU times, post-split top ten files, or three clean parallel runs. Consequently, the measured worker choice, two-minute file target, and panel reliability acceptance criteria remain unsubstantiated. My targeted run could not verify pipeline behavior because of the local dependency mismatch.
findings.failure_scenario: Under CPU contention, the panel test may still exceed its new deadline, or a split file may remain above the requested duration; the supplied change contains no measured results establishing either bound.

gold.summary: Unlimited quota still applies utilization reserves to free and metered providers.

findings.title: Honor unlimited quota for every billing type
findings.detail: Config accepts unlimited quota for free and metered providers, but this condition exempts only subscriptions. Other unlimited providers still lose headroom and become unavailable at their reserve. Reproduction: `bun test /private/tmp/lr-rMPEBN/claude-501/limitless-quota-review-1x5y39bf/quota-review.test.ts`. Output: `(fail) unlimited applies to a free enterprise CLI provider`; `Expected: 1`, `Received: -0.23749999999999993`.
findings.failure_scenario: Configure a Claude preset alias with billing="free" and quota="unlimited", then observe a five_hour window at 99%. The provider reports exhausted with reason "at reserve limit" and the router excludes it.

findings.title: Clear obsolete window alerts when enabling unlimited quota
findings.detail: The early return prevents new alerts but leaves persisted window alerts active after switching to unlimited. Neither startup reconciliation nor subsequent observations remove them. Reproduction: `bun test /private/tmp/lr-rMPEBN/claude-501/limitless-quota-review-1x5y39bf/quota-review.test.ts`. Output: `(fail) switching to unlimited removes informational window alerts`; expected `[]`, received an active five_hour exhausted alert with utilization 0.99 and resetsAt null.
findings.failure_scenario: A 99% window creates an alert without a reset timestamp. Restart with quota="unlimited" using the same database. The obsolete exhaustion alert remains visible indefinitely.

findings.title: Pre-existing config-cache regression test fails
findings.detail: The unchanged-worktree test consistently observes an extra config scan. Command: `bun test test/git-integrity.test.ts --test-name-pattern 'an unchanged worktree lists'`. Output: `Expected length: 1`, `Received length: 2`; `0 pass`, `1 fail`. The relevant implementation and test are unchanged by this diff.
findings.failure_scenario: Run the focused test against an unchanged fixture worktree; repeated Git commands produce two config listings rather than one.

gold.summary: A fixed review-time cutoff excludes worktrees created before the sidecar-writing release actually started.

findings.title: Use installation provenance instead of the upstream commit timestamp
findings.detail: The hardcoded cutoff assumes every installation deployed #323 when its upstream commit was created. An installation running the previous release after that timestamp produces genuine legacy worktrees that this migration excludes. Resume consequently skips registration and still fails with Missing trusted Git paths. Temporary regression command: bun test "$TMPDIR/review-357.test.ts". Output: '(fail) upgrade after upstream commit adopts the pre-upgrade run'; 'Expected: true'; 'Received: false'.
findings.failure_scenario: An installation still running the release before #323 successfully prepares and parks a run at timestamp 1791500000000, then upgrades directly to this change. Its missing record is never created.

findings.title: Support legacy local worktrees owned by the source repository
findings.detail: Registration always receives cachePath, but supported legacy local worktrees belong to the original source repository. Their factory bare cache may not exist, and registration fails while inspecting it. The existing local legacy test masks this case by explicitly creating a sidecar. Temporary regression command: bun test "$TMPDIR/review-357.test.ts". Output: '(fail) pre-upgrade local source-owned linked worktree is adopted'; 'error: Unsafe worktree Git administration'; 'ENOENT: no such file or directory, lstat .../repos/local-repo.git'.
findings.failure_scenario: A pre-upgrade local run has a valid linked worktree in the original source repository and no trusted-path record. Even when migration marks it legacy, resume fails because registration searches an unrelated bare cache.

gold.summary: Arbitrary assertion text mentioning a timeout is classified as a transient CI failure.
Retry eligibility ignores security failures outside the selected error line.
A paused PR is not inspected again when main recovers without another PR change.
An accepted rerun with a lost response is never reconciled to its later result.

findings.title: Compare repository URL components case-insensitively
findings.detail: GitHub repository names are case-insensitive, but this exact comparison rejects valid job responses whose canonical repository casing differs from the configured slug. Classification repeatedly throws before recording or rerunning the failure. Reproduction command: bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review-casing.ts". Output: {"reruns":0,"logs":["GitHub poll of o/r failed: Error: Incomplete failing job","GitHub poll of o/r failed: Error: Incomplete failing job"]}, followed by "Expected 1 rerun for canonical repository casing; received 0".
findings.failure_scenario: The configured repository is o/r, and GitHub returns https://api.github.com/repos/O/R/check-runs/11 for a valid timed-out job.

findings.title: Resume suppressed PR classification when main recovers
findings.detail: A main-red inspection clears ciPending. Subsequent inspection requires the PR's own CI state to change, so main recovering cannot resume reactions for an unchanged failing PR. The repository's red episode also remains stale. Reproduction command: bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review-recovery.ts". Output: {"restBeforeRecovery":4,"restAfterRecovery":4,"needsFix":0,"mainState":{"test":{"red":true,"episode":1}}}, followed by "Expected resumed classification with 1 ci.needs_fix after main recovered; received 0".
findings.failure_scenario: Main and a factory PR fail the same check. Main subsequently passes, but the PR remains failed at the same SHA with unchanged GraphQL contexts.

findings.title: Reconcile ambiguous rerun requests against later attempts
findings.detail: Only rerunning rows are reconciled. If GitHub accepts the POST but its response is lost, the durable row remains rerun_requested. A later successful attempt is ignored and ciPending is cleared, permanently losing the required flake evidence. Reproduction command: bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review-ambiguous.ts". Output: {"outcome":"rerun_requested","ciPending":false}, followed by "Expected confirmed later passing attempt to record failed_then_passed; received rerun_requested".
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub accepts a job rerun, the POST connection resets, and the rerun subsequently passes at the original SHA.

findings.title: Existing restart-repair test fails waiting for its pause callback
findings.detail: This unchanged test fails both in the full check and independently. Command: bun test test/pipeline.test.ts -t 'verify-change: restart-repair'. Output: "error: expect(received).toBeDefined()", "Received: undefined" at line 4304; "0 pass", "1 fail". Its fixed polling window expires before the expected repair pause is observed.
findings.failure_scenario: Running the restart-repair scenario in this checkout leaves resume undefined after 300 waits of 20 milliseconds.

gold.summary: Rate-limit refusals leave rerun claims unresolved across cooldowns and restarts.
ANSI-colored Bun failures and pytest security failures are missed by the retry exclusion.

findings.title: Isolate CI inspection errors from other PR observations
findings.detail: An exception from classifyCi escapes record and aborts the repository's observation loop. Later PRs' GraphQL observations are discarded, including merge events. A persistent inspection failure can therefore prevent unrelated PRs from being reconciled indefinitely. Regression command: `bun test /private/tmp/lr-eO88DH/claude-501/ci-review.test.ts`. The second test failed with `expect(received).not.toBeNull(); Received: null` for the later PR's saved observation.
findings.failure_scenario: Two factory PRs are observed in one repository. Fetching the first PR's CI logs returns HTTP 500, while the second PR has merged. The second PR's observation is never saved; repeated failures keep its merge unreconciled.

findings.title: Accept canonical repository casing in check-run URLs
findings.detail: The exact check_run_url comparison rejects valid GitHub responses when the configured repository spelling differs from GitHub's canonical casing. GitHub repository names are case-insensitive, and the surrounding details_url check already accommodates this. Inspection remains pending forever instead of classifying or rerunning the job. Regression command: `bun test /private/tmp/lr-eO88DH/claude-501/ci-review.test.ts`. The casing test failed with `Expected length: 1; Received length: 0` for rerun requests.
findings.failure_scenario: The stored slug is `o/r`, but a timed-out Actions job returns `https://api.github.com/repos/O/R/check-runs/11`. The classifier throws `Incomplete failing job` on every inspection and never requests the eligible rerun.

findings.title: Truncation overlap ignores longer escaped credential variants
findings.detail: redactCredentials now recognizes JSON-escaped variants, but overlap uses only literal credential lengths. When the runner cuts into an escaped variant, the remaining suffix can be longer than this overlap and survive redaction. findings.title: Restore a bounded diagnostic buffer
findings.detail: The previous 8,000-character per-line cap was removed without replacing it with a total character budget. Limiting the number of lines does not bound memory; once full, every additional diagnostic also joins and redacts the entire retained buffer. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {registerCredential} from "./src/util/proc.ts"; import {FailureExcerpts} from "./src/gates/failures.ts"; const e=new FailureExcerpts(); for(let i=0;i<39;i++) e.observe("x".repeat(1000000)); console.log("retained diagnostic characters:", (e as unknown as {lines:string[]}).lines.reduce((a,s)=>a+s.length,0));' Output: 'retained diagnostic characters: 39000000'.
findings.failure_scenario: A noisy gate prints repeated megabyte-sized newline-terminated diagnostics. The daemon retains tens or hundreds of megabytes and repeatedly copies them, potentially exhausting daemon memory despite the process output-tail limit.

gold.summary: The owner_diagnostics foreign keys cascade on delete without an index on event_id or invocation_id, so the daemon's synchronous debug-event cleanup scans the whole table for every deleted event and slows as owner rows grow.

findings.title: Raw diagnostics become agent-readable after rollback
findings.detail: Raw text persists in the shared SQLite database, but its read protection exists only in the new harness code. After rollback, the base release's editor profiles permit database reads: its Seatbelt profile has `(allow default)` and no read denial. The additive migration deliberately preserves these rows. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/owner-review-probes.ts"` produced `{"probe":"rollback database boundary","raw":{"text":"RAW_OWNER_HOLDOUT_MARKER"},"allowsDefault":true,"hasReadDenial":false}`. Real Seatbelt execution was unavailable inside this sandbox; the persisted row and base profile were checked directly.
findings.failure_scenario: The new release records verifier diagnostics, deployment rolls back to the base release, and an implementing agent reads owner_diagnostics directly from the database using its permitted filesystem access.

findings.title: Capture original thinking events before clipping
findings.detail: The owner copy is assembled from the normalized `message`. For thinking events, that message has already been clipped to 2,000 characters, so the new owner record cannot recover the full original diagnostic. A focused probe executed the actual onAgentEvent method with private text near the beginning and a diagnostic tail beyond the limit. `bun "$TMPDIR/owner-review-probes.ts"` produced `{"probe":"raw thinking event","inputLength":2136,"storedLength":2000,"tailPreserved":false}`.
findings.failure_scenario: A verifier emits a thinking event longer than 2,000 characters containing holdout text and useful diagnostic information near its end. show/logs display only the clipped owner copy.

findings.title: Prevent diagnostic ID reuse behind follow cursors
findings.detail: INTEGER PRIMARY KEY permits SQLite to reuse deleted maximum IDs. Debug-event cleanup cascades into this table, while logs -f advances using `id > diagnosticsAfter`. A new diagnostic can therefore receive an already-consumed ID and never print. `bun "$TMPDIR/owner-review-probes.ts"` reproduced cursor 1, deletion through deleteOldDebugEvents, a new run-error row with id 1, and `followRows:[]`.
findings.failure_scenario: logs -f consumes the latest diagnostic, associated with a debug event. GC removes that event and diagnostic (readily reproducible with debug_event_days = 0), then a new error diagnostic reuses its ID and is skipped by subsequent polling.

gold.summary: A resumed delivery whose base advanced again after a completed factory merge is refused, because the check requires the second merge's first parent to be the reviewed commit instead of the earlier factory merge.

findings.title: Do not authorize a changed merge commit from its parents alone
findings.detail: When pendingRebaseSha is set, this exception accepts any HEAD with the expected two parents. validateMerge checks ancestry, not the commit's tree or an exact recorded SHA. Amending a pending clean merge preserves those parents, so resume accepts the unreviewed amendment, reruns post-merge gates, and pushes it without review or audit. A temporary Git fixture invoking validateMerge after such an amendment printed: `validateMerge accepted amended, unreviewed HEAD: ce8e0282e9e7af6360d1efdead30a1c22a0656d6`.
findings.failure_scenario: Interrupt new-PR delivery during post-merge gates while pendingRebaseSha is persisted. Amend the merge commit to change a file without changing its parents, then resume. If the gates pass, the amended commit is pushed instead of ending needs_human.

findings.detail: Process-group membership is considered only when environment data is absent. A descendant with a readable replacement environment, such as env: {FOO: 'bar'}, has neither marker and is excluded even while remaining in the invocation's process group. findings.title: Working-directory heuristic selects unrelated processes for termination
findings.detail: A hidden orphan is classified as an invocation member solely because it was born after invocation start and has a cwd under an invocation root. gold.summary: The reader loopback policy cannot match the intended socket access.
An allow-default reader policy weakens the established confinement boundary.

findings.title: Restrict loopback binding to ephemeral ports
findings.detail: The wildcard network-bind rule permits binding any loopback TCP port. Restrictions on network-inbound prevent listening on service ports, but binding alone reserves a port and can prevent other local processes from using it. This violates the requested ephemeral-only restriction. The new test combines bind and listen, so a denial at listen hides the successful prohibited bind.
findings.failure_scenario: A verifier command binds an available 127.0.0.1:12345 socket and keeps it open without calling listen. Another local process attempting to start a service on that address receives EADDRINUSE despite the port being outside the permitted ephemeral range.

findings.title: Disable the HTTP idle timeout for long-running reader commands
findings.detail: Bun.serve defaults to a 10-second idle timeout. This endpoint uses enableJsonResponse and awaits the entire command before sending its response, so even commands producing subprocess output send no HTTP traffic while running. Commands exceeding the HTTP idle window lose their connection; req.signal also participates in command cancellation. The configured command and MCP timeouts therefore cannot protect ordinary longer test runs.
findings.failure_scenario: A verifier invokes a local-server test suite taking 30 seconds with timeoutMs and idleTimeoutMs both set to 180000. The MCP connection times out before the command returns, preventing the verifier from receiving the test result.

findings.detail: The global checks.every(passed) rejects every substitution when any gate contains a skipped test, even when retained coverage proves the required loopback file passed without skips. This repository deliberately skips nested Seatbelt tests inside confined gates, so its normal successful gate run cannot supply evidence for the blocked loopback verification. The original needs_human failure therefore persists. The verifier reports the loopback test blocked by its sandbox. Substitution refuses the passing gate evidence and verification ends as needs_human.

findings.title: Old local-repo worktrees can't be recorded
findings.detail: `recordLegacyWorktree` always uses `cachePath(deps.cfg.paths, ctx.repo)` and requires that repository to be bare and to list the worktree. Older local-repo worktrees were added from the user's source repository. The engine supports them elsewhere through `worktreeOwner`, and the test 'an interrupted legacy worktree finishes in its owner while new runs use the clone' covers that case. For such a run with no record, the cache may not exist or may not list the worktree, so registration throws 'Unsafe worktree Git administration' instead of recording it.
findings.failure_scenario: A local-repo run whose worktree was added from `repo.localPath` by an older release (no sidecar) is marked legacy. On resume, `lstat` of the missing local cache throws, or the fields[1]==='bare' or listing check fails. The run fails with 'Unsafe worktree Git administration'.

gold.summary: Rate-limit refusals leave rerun claims unresolved across cooldowns and restarts.
ANSI-colored Bun failures and pytest security failures are missed by the retry exclusion.

findings.title: A persistent classifier exception on one PR starves every later PR in the repo batch, merges included
findings.detail: `classifyCi` throws on many conditions (`Incomplete CI inspection` for any non-200 status, `Incomplete failing check`, `Ambiguous originating CI job`, `Outdated CI check completion`, and so on). It runs inside `record()`, which runs inside the `for (const [i, pr] of known.entries())` loop in `observe()`. The throw unwinds `observe()`, which `tick` catches per repository, so no later PR in that batch is recorded. The PR that threw was already saved with `ciPending: true`, and `(same && prev?.ciPending)` keeps it pending, so the same throw recurs on every poll. The starvation lasts until that PR's head or CI changes. The base code had no such path.
findings.failure_scenario: Probe test (in TMPDIR) with PR #1 failing the check `test`, where its job log returns 410 Gone, and PR #2 in the same repo becoming MERGED. After 40 polls (10 minutes of fake time), the logs show `GitHub poll of o/r failed: Error: Incomplete CI inspection: actions/jobs/7/logs (410)` on every cycle,

findings.title: Main-red pause re-fetches REST on every poll although GraphQL is unchanged
findings.detail: When a PR's failing check is red on main, `classifyCi` returns false (`paused`). `ciPending` therefore stays persisted, and every later poll re-runs the classification: GET commits/main, the main check-runs pages, and the PR check-runs pages, even when the GraphQL `ciKey` is identical. The request says to fetch failing check runs and jobs by REST "only when the GraphQL state changed". Delivered PRs poll every 15 s, which is roughly 720 or more REST calls per hour per paused PR. Several PRs blocked by one red main can use up the 5000/h budget that the poller and the rest of the factory share.
findings.failure_scenario: Probe test: one PR fails `test` and main's check `test` is also failing. After the first poll there were 4 REST calls. After 10 more polls with unchanged GraphQL there were 34: commits/main, main check-runs and PR check-runs on every cycle.

findings.title: Failure signature can pick a passing test or setup line, and it includes run timings
findings.detail: `ciSignature` takes the first log line matching `/timed out after|##\[error\]|\b(?:error|fail(?:ed|ure)?)\b/i`. Passing test names containing 'error' or 'fail', and action inputs such as `continue-on-error: false` or `fail-on-cache-miss`, match before the actual failure. Lines also keep durations such as `[5000.01ms]`, so the same failure produces a different signature on every run. The ledger's "failing test or error line" is then wrong, unrelated failures in one job collapse into one signature (the cap is over-applied, and needs_fix items are deduplicated away), and identical failures never aggregate across runs.
findings.failure_scenario: `ciSignature('test', log, 'x')` on a log with '(pass) parser > returns an error on invalid input [1.20ms]' followed by '(fail) store > persists rows [3.10ms]' returns line '(pass) parser > returns an error on invalid input [1.20ms]'. Verified with bun.

findings.title: Fail-fast cancelled matrix jobs are treated as transient, rerun, and recorded as flakes
findings.detail: Any check or job with conclusion `cancelled` is classified as transient, unless the remote head has moved. The request covers a *run* cancelled without being superseded. In a matrix with fail-fast, a real failure in one job cancels its siblings at the same SHA. Those cancelled siblings get rerun, and when the rerun passes, `failed_then_passed` is written to the ledger as nondeterminism evidence, although nothing was nondeterministic. The rerun budget is also spent for nothing. The test 'eligible cancelled failure reruns only its job' locks this behaviour in.
findings.failure_scenario: Matrix run with jobs `test (a)` (conclusion failure, assertion error) and `test (b)` (conclusion cancelled by fail-fast). `test (b)` is rerun via jobs/{id}/rerun, passes, and the ledger row becomes `failed_then_passed`.

findings.title: record() now drops the whole PR observation when the head epoch check refuses
findings.detail: The base code called `store.observePrHead(pr.url, head, since)` and still saved the snapshot and emitted feed items. The change returns early when that call returns false, which happens while a round is pushing or when the version has moved. During that window pr.merged, pr.closed, review and comment events for the PR are not recorded. This change in behaviour is outside the CI scope and is untested.
findings.failure_scenario: A review round is mid-push (pr_heads.pushing set to a running run) when the PR is merged or receives a review. The poll that observes it discards the whole observation, and no state or feed item is saved for that cycle.

findings.title: Feed excerpt is the first 2000 chars of the job log (runner setup), not the failure
findings.detail: `emit(..., log || f.line)` passes the whole job log, and `excerpt.trim().slice(0, 2000)` keeps its head. GitHub Actions job logs begin with runner, image and setup output, so for any realistic log the excerpt contains no failure information.
findings.failure_scenario: A typical 50 KB job log whose failure is near the end produces a ci.needs_fix item whose excerpt is only 'Current runner version...', 'Runner Image...' and setup lines.

findings.title: Multiple transient jobs in one run are rerun one by one; later POSTs may be rejected and reported as needs_fix
findings.detail: Each eligible job gets its own POST to `actions/jobs/{id}/rerun`. After the first one, the run is in progress again, and GitHub may refuse a second job rerun on a running run. A 4xx response is treated as a definitive `rerun_rejected` followed by needs_fix. The request says "Rerun the failed jobs", and `runs/{id}/rerun-failed-jobs` does that in one call. I could not verify GitHub's live behaviour here.
findings.failure_scenario: Two matrix jobs in the same run both time out. The first rerun returns 201. The second may return 403 while the run is in progress, and is marked rerun_rejected with a needs_fix item.

findings.title: Two migrations for one new, unshipped table; change is about twice the source-line budget
findings.detail: `rerun_job` is added by a second ALTER migration, although the table is created in the same change. The source diff is about 560 lines against a budget of about 250, with a 411-line classifier that is hard to audit.
findings.failure_scenario: Not applicable: this is a maintainability issue with no runtime failure.

gold.summary: Retrying an unchanged run converts inherited model chains into explicit overrides.
Routing previews remain stale after quota or cooldown expiry without an event.
Clearing a default effort omits the field from PATCH and leaves the old value stored.
Catalog history disappears on reload and does not include changes made by another client.

findings.title: New Playwright dependency and a postinstall that downloads Chromium per install
findings.detail: The diff adds `playwright` as a devDependency, changing bun.lock, plus a root `postinstall` that runs `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=0 playwright install chromium-headless-shell`. With PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=0 the browser lands inside each checkout's node_modules, so nothing is shared between installs. This repo's .limitless.toml setup gate (and CI) runs `bun install --frozen-lockfile` in every factory worktree, so every run on this repo now downloads a Chromium build from the Playwright CDN. If that CDN is unreachable, the postinstall exits non-zero and the setup gate fails. The request asked for UI tests with fake API responses following the existing patterns. It did not ask for a real-browse
findings.failure_scenario: A factory run on this repo in a worktree without access to the Playwright CDN: the `bun install --frozen-lockfile` setup gate fails in postinstall, and the run fails before any work starts. With network access, each run downloads Chromium into its own node_modules instead.

findings.title: Retry with different models pins every role to the current policy chain when the run had no chains
findings.detail: When run.models is empty, RetryModels fetches /api/routing and prefills every role with `effective[role][run.complexity ?? 'medium']` (or the default cell). Submitting sends all of them as the replacement map. RuntimePolicy treats a run chain as overriding every cell for that role. So the retried run ignores complexity-based routing and any later operator or evals changes, for every role, including roles the operator never touched. The request says the picker opens 'prefilled with the run's chains'.
findings.failure_scenario: A policy-routed run (models = {}) failed. The operator opens Retry with different models, changes only `implement`, and submits. The body pins triage, spec, review, verify and the rest to their medium-cell chains. Those roles in the retried run no longer follow the large/small cells or later operato

findings.title: Every provider SSE event triggers a full Setup reload of about 20 requests
findings.detail: refresh() runs on every 'provider' message. ProviderTracker publishes a provider message on every slot acquire and release and on each quota window observation. Each refresh calls GET /api/routing, /api/catalog, /api/providers and /api/stats/providers (a DB aggregate), plus one /api/routing/preview per role×cell (16 with DEFAULT_POLICY). There is no debounce or coalescing.
findings.failure_scenario: With several concurrent runs, every agent invocation start and end sends about 20 HTTP requests from each open Setup tab, including a workload-stats aggregate.

findings.title: Catalog change history exists only for the open tab and has no change note
findings.detail: The request asks History to show recent routing and catalog changes (what, old → new, note, when). Catalog changes are only appended to a client-side `session` signal. Catalog changes made in another tab, via the CLI, or before a reload never appear. The CatalogForm 'Note (optional)' field writes the model's persistent `notes` attribute rather than a change note.
findings.failure_scenario: The operator adds a runtime model, reloads /setup, and the History section no longer shows the addition.

findings.title: Change is far over the ~450 source-line budget, and the test harness rewrites source with regexes
findings.detail: UI and source changes total about 1,300 lines (Setup.tsx alone is 632) against a budget of about 450. The new test harness (setup-ui-support.ts) rewrites component source with string and regex replacements, for example replacing the last `\n  return (` and the `export const X =` declarations. Small formatting changes to the components will break it.
findings.failure_scenario: A future refactor that adds an early `return (` to Setup.tsx silently breaks the harness's render extraction.

gold.summary: Unicode and URL encodings evade privacy protection in status and digest fields.

findings.title: Digest lists a PR as awaiting review while a requested-changes round is still running
findings.detail: The group-1 (PRs awaiting review) test only checks handled/closed status, the approval and the land entry. It never looks at `detail.review.rounds`. A "changes" verdict marks the approval stale and queues a round run, so the original run's `run.pr_opened` item still passes `(!approval || approval.stale ...)` and is counted as awaiting review even though the factory is still pushing fixes. `explainStatus` in the same change handles this case and reports "Review changes in progress", so the two new surfaces disagree. A fresh session that trusts the digest may review or approve a head that is about to move. The approve path in submitReview does not check for an active round.
findings.failure_scenario: Probe (test in TMPDIR): run A has status succeeded, prUrl set, PR OPEN at head sha, review.approval {sha, stale:true}, and one round with status 'running'. The feed has one run.pr_opened item. Digest output: 'Needs you: 0; PRs awaiting review: 1; Blocked lands: 0'. explainStatus on the same detail r

findings.title: MCP review verdicts are attributed to reviewer "human"
findings.detail: The MCP review tool strips `reviewer`, and submitReview defaults it to "human". Approvals made by an AI agent through MCP are stored in review_approvals as reviewer=human, and the review.approved feed item says "approved ... by human". Other paths label their source: the CLI sends `reviewer: $USER`, and the MCP answer tool sends `by: "mcp"`. This breaks the audit trail for who approved a PR before landing.
findings.failure_scenario: An agent calls limitless_review {verdict:'approve'}. The approval row's reviewer is 'human', and the feed reads '... approved at abc by human'.

findings.title: Digest item lines are unbounded in length
findings.detail: Each row quotes the full title and summary. `run.failed` and `run.needs_human` summaries come from `run.error`, and question summaries are the full question text. JSON quoting keeps each on one line, but a single line can be many kilobytes of untrusted error, CI or question text. The SessionStart hook injects all of it into every new session's context. The 20-line cap does not bound the output size.
findings.failure_scenario: A run fails with a 20 KB error or stack trace. Every session start then injects a 20 KB digest line.

findings.title: limitless_status returns no state or next action when the private-strings file is unreadable
findings.detail: When loadPrivateStrings throws, the tool returns only `{land:{id,state}, openQuestions}`. The `state` and `nextAction` strings are fixed templates that include at most a run id, so dropping them is not needed for privacy. The result also gives no hint that output was withheld or why. An agent calling the status verb gets an object with no state and no guidance.
findings.failure_scenario: ~/.config/limitless/private-strings.txt is a directory or contains invalid UTF-8. limitless_status then returns {land:null, openQuestions:0}, with no state or next action.

gold.summary: Smoke invocations do not honor the configured model-origin exclusions.

findings.title: Eval resume doesn't refuse excluded models in a stored switch chain up front
findings.detail: `resume()` checks each stored switchChains target with `router.resolveFor('implement', target)`, which never consults `excludeOrigins`. A fresh submit builds its chain from `policyTargets`, which drops excluded models, but a resume reuses the predecessor's stored chain. If `exclude_origins` was added after the original eval ran, the resume is accepted. The excluded model is only caught when `nextImplementTarget` calls `router.toTarget`, which throws after round one has already run on another model, so that trial ends in an error instead of being refused with the reason before any trial starts. The excluded model is never called, so safety holds, but this doesn't match the 'refused up front'
findings.failure_scenario: Run an implement eval with strategy=switch, where the policy includes a CN model, while exclude_origins is unset. Interrupt it, add `exclude_origins = ["CN"]`, restart and resume it. The resume is accepted, round one runs, and the switch step then fails the trial with an error instead of the resume

findings.title: Private-output no-capacity message repeats the same origin reason
findings.detail: The run-log warning deduplicates the origin reasons with `new Set`, but the `privateOutput` NoCapacityError message joins the raw `origins` array. When several CN models are skipped, it repeats `origin excluded (CN; baseOrigin=CN)` once per skipped model.
findings.failure_scenario: A privateOutput invocation where three CN models are skipped produces 'No model available for X. origin excluded (CN; baseOrigin=CN), origin excluded (CN; baseOrigin=CN), origin excluded (CN; baseOrigin=CN)'.

gold.summary: The isolated post-check status still inspects populated submodules with their own git directories, so a submodule that points at the land clone's admin directory runs a clean filter from the clone's configuration, which the request says never applies after the checks.

findings.title: The pager scenario can never trigger the pager, and `--no-pager` is untested
findings.detail: The `checks:pager` scenario plants `core.pager` and `pager.status`, but the script captures status output with `dirty="$(...)"`, and the test runs without a pseudo-terminal. Git only starts a pager when stdout is a terminal, so no marker could run even with the old in-clone status or with `--no-pager` removed. The request asked for a pseudo-terminal or, failing that, an assertion that `GIT_PAGER` or `--no-pager` is used. The test does neither, so removing the new `--no-pager` from `safe_git` would not fail any test. Only the general 'post-check git uses the private dir' assertion covers isolation here.
findings.failure_scenario: Delete `--no-pager` from `safe_git` in `scripts/land-pr.sh`, then run `bun test test/land-pr.test.ts -t checks:pager`. It still passes.

findings.title: Writing `info/exclude` fails when git init uses an empty template directory
findings.detail: The line `printf '%s' "$exclude" > "$push_repo/info/exclude"` assumes `git init --bare` created `info/`. That directory comes from the init template. With an empty template (for example a global `init.templateDir` pointing at an empty directory, or `--template=`), `info/` does not exist. I confirmed that `git init --bare --template=` creates only HEAD, config, objects and refs. The redirect then fails, `set -e` aborts the land with a raw shell error, and this step skips the script's usual checked-step handling with a generic message.
findings.failure_scenario: A user whose global gitconfig sets `init.templateDir` to an empty directory runs `scripts/land-pr.sh`. The land aborts with 'No such file or directory' after the checks pass.

findings.title: The dirty check still spawns git inside populated submodules, which applies their own config
findings.detail: `status` in the private repository recurses into any gitlink whose directory holds a `.git`, running `git status` there. That child process reads the submodule's own config. `safe_git` only blanks `filter.*` and `hook.*` keys found in the private repository's config, so a `filter.<x>.clean` planted in the submodule's config still runs. I reproduced this: a populated submodule with `filter.x.clean = "touch MARKER; cat"` and a matching attribute created MARKER during `status --porcelain` from an isolated bare repository. The old in-clone status had the same behaviour, and the audit flags gitlinks unless submodules are allowed, so the risk is limited. Still, the request's claim that filter conf
findings.failure_scenario: A PR commits a gitlink `sub`. Its checks run `git init sub` and set `filter.x.clean` in `sub/.git/config`, plus an `info/attributes` file matching a file in `sub`. The post-check status then runs the clean command.

findings.title: Fresh index without stat data makes smudged LFS files look modified
findings.detail: After `read-tree`, the private index has no stat data, so `status` hashes every work-tree file. `safe_git` blanks every `filter.*` key, including the global `filter.lfs.*` ones, so files that LFS smudged on checkout hash to their real contents, not their pointer blobs. They therefore show as modified and the land is refused. The old in-clone status used an index with cached stat data and would not have hashed them. This repository has no tracked `.gitattributes` or LFS files today, so there is no current impact.
findings.failure_scenario: A clone with an LFS-tracked file checked out through the global git-lfs smudge filter runs land-pr.sh. The land is refused with 'Worktree differs from landing commit'.

gold.summary: Unavailable-target diagnostics expose registered credentials in routing API and Setup output.

findings.title: Any unknown stored prefer entry is now silently dropped and mislabelled as a 'retired reference'
findings.detail: `retiredReason(id, providers)` treats every prefer entry that is not a provider id as retired. That includes a model id stored by mistake, such as "codex/sol". Before this change startup refused it with a helpful message ('is a model ID, not a provider; prefer takes provider IDs (use "codex")'). Now it is filtered out and the warning says 'retired reference: codex/sol is not in the catalog', which is false because codex/sol is in the catalog as a model. The base test assertions for this case and for the history count were deleted rather than adapted.
findings.failure_scenario: An older release stored routing.prefer = ["codex/sol"]. On startup the preference is dropped with the warning 'codex/sol: unavailable (retired reference: codex/sol is not in the catalog); prefer', which misleads the operator about the cause.

findings.title: Stored evals and run retries that name the removed model still cannot be resumed
findings.detail: The request says records written before the change 'still render and resume'. Eval resume re-validates the stored request and returns 400 'unknown model ID' for the removed model, and the new test asserts that failure. `Factory.retryRun` also re-validates inherited `run.models`. A historical run pinned to `[retired, live]` fails to retry with `models.implement entry "retired-lan/legacy": Error: unknown model ID`, which I reproduced with a probe test. Interrupted runs do resume, because the router skips unknown ids. This matches how earlier removed models (codex/astra) were handled, so it is not a regression, but it is weaker than the request's wording.
findings.failure_scenario: An interrupted eval whose request is ["<removed model>@none", "codex/sol@low"] cannot be resumed. A failed run pinned with implement=["<removed model>", "codex/sol"] cannot be retried without new explicit pins.

findings.title: remote_host is parsed as a URL, so some SSH destination forms crash or never match a provider
findings.detail: `new URL(`http://${host}:8080`)` throws on some SSH destination forms, e.g. `gpu:2222` or `ssh://gpu:2222`, and the CLI exits with an uncaught 'TypeError: Invalid URL'. When remote_host is an SSH alias that differs from the provider's URL host (an ~/.ssh/config alias vs an IP), no provider matches. The health probe then runs without authentication and reports 'unreachable', and up/down silently skip the enable/disable toggle. Enablement matching is documented in OPERATIONS.md, but the crash is not handled.
findings.failure_scenario: With `[local] remote_host = "gpu:2222"`, `limitless local status` throws TypeError: Invalid URL. I confirmed this with `bun -e` against manageLocal.

findings.title: Catalog-edit validation was relaxed beyond retired references, and the change is over budget
findings.detail: `apply()` now validates only references to the edited id that were valid before the edit. Every other already-invalid reference is ignored, not just retired ones, in all layers: code, evals, operator and runs. The test 'catalog POST refuses a retained invalid %s reference' was inverted to 'tolerates'. Re-adding a model under an id that stored chains already reference skips validating those chains, because they were invalid before the add. Together with the Setup.tsx UI additions and the new `unavailable` snapshot fields, source changes are about 250 lines against the requested ~120.
findings.failure_scenario: A stored run chain names "codex/x@high" while codex/x does not exist. An operator POSTs a runtime model codex/x that supports only ["none"]. The add succeeds without checking the run chain, which now holds an unsupported effort that is only discovered when routing.

gold.summary: JSON escaping lets ordinary logged credentials evade literal gate-output redaction.
Line callbacks store pieces of multiline credentials in failure excerpts.

findings.title: Change is far over its budget and redacts at many consumers instead of once at the source
findings.detail: The request said: redact gate output once, where `runGates` builds the result, about 30 net source lines, so every consumer gets redacted text from one place. The diff changes about 115 source lines. On top of the source fix it adds: `redactGateData` (a JSON round-trip that also rewrites objects) applied to every HTTP JSON and SSE payload; re-serialization of the artifact endpoint; redaction of `RunContext` state in the constructor; redaction in `renderReport`, `implementPrompt`, `reviewPrompt`, `verifyPrompt` and `formatGateOutput`; per-stream truncation flags in `ProcResult`; and new `confinementError` semantics (now always written, and when it is false, `confinementFailed` no longer scans
findings.failure_scenario: Any reviewer comparing the diff against the issue: 18 files and about 115 source lines changed against a stated budget of about 30, with changes to the API and run state that the issue did not ask for.

findings.title: Artifact endpoint now rewrites stored artifacts (minifies JSON, adds fields, strips control sequences)
findings.detail: `redactGateArtifact` parses every artifact as JSON and re-serializes it through `redactGateData`. Pretty-printed artifacts such as `baseline-gates.json` and `gates-N.json` (written with `JSON.stringify(x, null, 2)`) are now served minified. Any object that has `ok` and `output` also gets a `confinementError` field that was never stored. Artifacts that are not JSON (`diff.patch`, `report.md`, `spec.md`) go through `stripVTControlCharacters`, so the patch served is not byte-identical to the stored one. Probe output: `{"checks":[{"name":"t","ok":true,"output":"fine","confinementError":false}]}` from a pretty-printed input without that field.
findings.failure_scenario: GET /api/runs/:id/artifacts/gates-1.json returns one minified line with an added confinementError field instead of the stored pretty-printed JSON. GET …/diff.patch on a change that adds ESC sequences returns a patch without them.

findings.title: Review prompt input is ANSI-stripped, so the reviewer sees a different patch than the one under review
findings.detail: `reviewPrompt` now runs its whole input through `redactGateData`, which applies `stripVTControlCharacters` to every string, including the inline `patch`, the request `prompt` and the implementer report. Terminal escape sequences that a change adds to source or fixtures disappear from the diff the reviewer reads. A reviewer can then neither see nor flag them, e.g. terminal-injection content in output strings. This goes beyond gate output, which was the only scope of the request.
findings.failure_scenario: Under PR verification, a diff adds `console.log("\x1b]0;pwned\x07")` as raw ESC/BEL bytes. The patch in the review prompt shows the line without the escape sequence, so the reviewer approves what looks like a harmless log line.

findings.title: `confinementError` now always serialized, reversing the documented 'present only when set' convention
findings.detail: The removed comment said the field was 'Present only when set, like timedOut, so results stay readable by strict schemas and older releases.' Every result now carries `confinementError: false`, and `confinementFailed` uses `??`, so an explicit false overrides the output scan. Both changes support the 'redaction could hide the diagnostic' edge case, which the raw line scan already covered without changing what is persisted.
findings.failure_scenario: A tool with a strict schema for gate results, of the kind the removed comment warned about, rejects rows that now carry `confinementError: false`.

gold.summary: An incomplete terminal escape consumes part of a credential before it can be matched.
Terminal-control stripping changes with chunk boundaries and loses state at the hold limit.

findings.title: Deploy gate redaction does nothing in production: the deploy CLI process never registers credentials
findings.detail: The `deploy` case in src/cli/main.ts imports ./service.ts and calls svc.deploy without calling loadConfig(). registerCredential is called only from src/config.ts:182 (inside loadConfig), and neither service.ts nor its imports load config. So in a real `limitless deploy` process the credential set is empty, and both `redactOutput: true` and `redactGateStreams` return the text unchanged. The deploy error still contains any provider API key a check prints. The new deploy tests call registerCredential themselves in the test process, which hides the gap.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator runs `limitless deploy --smoke`. A test in the release checkout fails and prints the provider API key from the environment or a fixture. registeredCredentials() is empty in that CLI process, so the thrown deploy error and the console show the key unredacted.

findings.title: About 4.7x over the line budget, and redaction is spread across many places instead of the single point requested
findings.detail: The issue asks for gate output to be redacted once, where runGates builds a check's result, so that every consumer receives redacted text from that one place. The budget is about 30 net source lines. The diff adds 140 net source lines and also redacts in: every HTTP JSON response and SSE message (`serialize`), the artifact endpoint (re-parsing and re-serializing every artifact), RunContext state on load, checkpoint reads, implementPrompt, reviewPrompt, verifyPrompt, formatGateFeedback, renderReport and formatGateOutput. It also adds JSON-escaped credential variants, per-stream truncation flags and a change to the MCP privacy policy. AGENTS.md says to stay within the issue's line budget and t
findings.failure_scenario: Every API response and SSE event is now stringified, parsed and stringified again, with every string VT-stripped and scanned for credentials. That is extra cost and behavior change on all endpoints, for a request that only covered gate output.

findings.title: MCP/digest privacy now hides any text containing "[redacted]", with no test
findings.detail: `text.includes("[redacted]")` now replaces the whole string with "[withheld: private text]". Harness-redacted agent output, run titles or review findings that mention the marker, and gate output that is now redacted all lose their full text in MCP tools and the digest. Before, they passed through with only the credential replaced. No test was added for this policy change.
findings.failure_scenario: A run's gate output is "credential: [redacted]\n(fail) assertion ...". An MCP client reading the run's gates gets "[withheld: private text]" in place of the whole diagnostic.

findings.title: redactGateData strips terminal control characters from every string and adds confinementError to unrelated payloads
findings.detail: redactGateData is now applied to all HTTP responses, non-JSON artifacts (for example diff.patch, through redactGateOutput), the review prompt's inline patch and the user prompt. It strips VT control characters from all of them, which changes content beyond credential redaction. It also adds `confinementError` to any object that has `ok` and `output` keys, whether or not it is a GateResult.
findings.failure_scenario: A patch that adds a file containing literal ESC bytes is served by /api/runs/:id/artifacts/diff.patch with those bytes removed, so it no longer applies cleanly.
